#71 TABATABAI d.1402 · holds · Al-Tabataba'i treats these similar stories as applications of the verses, not separate revelation occasions: the sura came down all at once, and the same proposal may have recurred. «إنما هي من قبيل ما نسميه تطبيقا بمعنى أنهم وجدوا مضامين بعض الآيات تقبل الانطباق على بعض القصص الواقعة» [filed under 6:52, 6:53]
#72 TABATABAI d.1402 · holds · Reports giving occasions of revelation for this Meccan surah often relate events merely associated with the verses; paraphrase, weak transmission, and fabrication prevent treating them as exclusive causes. «فلا اعتماد في أمثال هذه السورة من السور التي نزلت دفعة»
#73 TABATABAI d.1402 · عمر بن عبد الله بن المهاجر · reports · A report says the verse came after some people proposed that the Prophet expel the poor Companions of the Suffa. «عن عمر بن عبد الله بن المهاجر أن الآية نزلت في اقتراح بعض الناس»
#74 TABATABAI d.1402 · rejects · He rejects that as a specific occasion because the surah was revealed all at once in Mecca, before the Hijra. «ويضعفه ما تقدم في نظيره أن السورة إنما نزلت دفعة وفي مكة قبل الهجرة»
#75 TABATABAI d.1402 · holds · Reports assigning preceding verses to enemies of the Prophet’s family are applications or inner interpretations, not occasions of revelation, given the surah’s Meccan, single-period descent. «والظاهر أنها جميعا من قبيل الجري والتطبيق أو الأخذ بباطن المعنى» [filed under 6:52, 6:54]
#76 TABATABAI d.1402 · holds · God has no bodily face or material direction; “face” is what something faces others with, so it can metaphorically denote the direction or aspect by which it is encountered. «لكن وجه الشيء لما كان ما يستقبل به غيره كانت الجهة بمعنى الناحية»
#77 TABATABAI d.1402 · holds · Righteous works can be a face oriented toward God, while evil works face Satan; divine attributes and names are also ways creation encounters God. «وبهذه العناية تصير الأعمال الصالحة وجها لله تعالى كما أن الأعمال الطالحة وجه للشيطان»
#78 TABATABAI d.1402 · holds · The phrase “possessor of majesty and honor” grammatically describes the face, not the Lord, in the verse about God's enduring face. «فإن ظاهر الآية أن قوله { ذو الجلال والإكرام } نعت للوجه دون الرب»
#79 TABATABAI d.1402 · holds · Anything related to divine nearness—God's names, attributes, religion, good deeds, prophets, angels, martyrs, and forgiven believers—is a face of God. «وكذا كل من يحل في ساحة قربه كالأنبياء والملائكة والشهداء وكل مغفور له من المؤمنين وجه له تعالى»
#80 TABATABAI d.1402 · holds · These near-to-God realities endure by God's permanence; “everything perishes except His face” identifies them as remaining in His secure presence. «فدل الحصر الذي في الآية على أن ذلك كله وجه لله سبحانه»
#81 TABATABAI d.1402 · holds · What worshippers seek from God is His face, including divine favor, mercy, satisfaction, and the means of nearness to Him. «فكل ذلك وجهه تعالى لأن صفات فعله تعالى كالرحمة والمرضاة والفضل ونحو ذلك من وجهه»
#82 TABATABAI d.1402 · holds · “Account” originally denotes numerical reckoning and extends to measuring deeds for recompense; because reward is God's, the reckoning is His responsibility. «فالحساب على الله تعالى أي في عهدته وكفايته»
#83 TABATABAI d.1402 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم · reports · A report calls those who deny divine decree and claim independent human will and power the Magians of this community. «قال فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم " ألا إن لكل أمه مجوسا»
#84 TABATABAI d.1402 · holds · Al-Tabataba'i explains the hadith as condemning those who deny God's relation to human acts and make humans independent creators, like Zoroastrian dualism. «وهو أن لإرادة الله سبحانه تعلقا ما بأعمال العباد»
#85 TABATABAI d.1402 · المعتزلة · reports · The Mu'tazilites reinterpret the hadith to target those who affirm decree, claiming they resemble Magians by assigning good and evil to a creator other than humans. «وقد أول المعتزلة وهم النافون للقدر الرواية بأن المراد بالقدرية المثبتون للقدر»
#86 TABATABAI d.1402 · rejects · The manuscript readings that combine “no decree” with denial of human will contradict each other, so al-Tabataba'i attributes that combination to scribal corruption. «والقول بالقدر يلازم القول بنفي استقلاله بالمشيئة والقدرة»
#87 TABATABAI d.1402 · عبد الله بن مسعود · reports · Ibn Mas'ud reports that Quraysh leaders asked the Prophet to expel poor Muslims such as Suhayb, Ammar, Bilal, and Khabbab so they might follow him. «مر الملأ من قريش على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وعنده صهيب وعمار وبلال وخباب» [filed under 6:51, 6:52]
#88 TABATABAI d.1402 · بعض المفسرين · reports · Some commentators say the people singled out are believers who affirm resurrection and are the poor believers mentioned in the next verse. «في المؤمنين القائلين بالحشر، وأنهم هم الذين عنوا في الآية التالية» [filed under 6:51, 6:52]
#89 TABATABAI d.1402 · holds · The context indicates that Meccan polytheists asked the Prophet to expel poor believers; this resembles elites in Noah's community demanding the same of him. «أن المشركين من قومه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم اقترحوا عليه أن يطرد عن نفسه الضعفاء المؤمنين به» [filed under 6:52, 6:53]
#90 ASAD-NOTES d.1412 · reports · Traditions place the revelation of this and the next verse after Meccan pagan leaders offered to consider Islam if Muhammad dismissed former slaves and other low-status followers; he rejected their demand. «some of the pagan chieftains at Mecca expressed their willingness to consider accepting Islam on the condition»
#91 ASAD-NOTES d.1412 · holds · Asad says the historical occasion is not a full explanation: the verse's wording concerns people who believe in God and seek His grace, even if they are not Muslims in the current sense. «while not being Muslims in the current sense of this word»
#92 ASAD-NOTES d.1412 · holds · The enduring instruction applies to all Qur'an followers: do not repel anyone who believes in God, even with incomplete Qur'anic beliefs; instead explain the teaching patiently. «they are enjoined not to repulse anyone who believes in God - even though his beliefs may not fully answer»
#93 ASAD-NOTES d.1412 · holds · The reciprocal accountability clause means people answer to God alone for beliefs or conduct that differ from Qur'anic teaching. «all are accountable to God alone»
#94 ASAD-NOTES d.1412 · holds · The literal phrase means that repelling them would make the addressee one of the evildoers. «so that thou shouldst repulse them and thus be of the evildoers»
#95 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · In the four-sūrah sequence, al-An‘ām conclusively presents truth to Quraysh, while al-A‘rāf warns them. «Sūrah al-An‘ām conclusively communicates the truth to the Quraysh. Sūrah al-A‘rāf sounds a warning to them.» [filed under 6:1-165]
#96 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · Al-Anfāl prepares believers for jihād and announces Quraysh's removal from custodianship of the House of God. «the divine decision is taken to depose the Quraysh from the custodianship of the House of God.» [filed under 6:1-165]
#97 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · Al-Tawbah issues Quraysh an ultimatum and gives the Hypocrites a final warning. «an ultimatum is sounded to the Quraysh and the Hypocrites are given a final warning.» [filed under 6:1-165]
#98 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · Qur’an Group 1 primarily addresses the People of the Book and only secondarily Quraysh; Group 2 reverses that order. «Group 1 of the Qur’ ān is directed to the People of the Book. If the Quraysh are addressed, it is only in a secondary way.» [filed under 6:1-165]
#99 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · Group 2 argues mainly from human nature, intellect, and the world, whereas Group 1 uses matters the People of the Book acknowledged. «In Group 2, arguments are mostly drawn from the signs found in human nature and intellect and in the world around human beings.» [filed under 6:1-165]
#100 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · In Group 1 believers replace the People of the Book as religious leaders; in Group 2 they replace Quraysh as custodians of the House. «In Group 1, the People of the Book are deposed from religious leadership and their place has been given to the believers.» [filed under 6:1-165]
#101 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · The sūrah invites Quraysh to monotheism, the hereafter, and Muhammad’s prophethood, warning them with the fate of nations that rejected messengers and using Abraham’s argument to identify his true followers. «They are invited to profess faith while arguments in favour of monotheism, the hereafter» [filed under 6:1-165]
#102 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · This section tells Muhammad to leave sign-demanders, warn those fearing God and the hereafter, and preserve access for poor believers rather than appease arrogant elites. «those who were demanding signs and punishments. However, he should warn through this book those who fear God and the hereafter.» [filed under 6:51-55]
#103 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · The believers seeking religious understanding are worthy of the Prophet’s attention, while the poor’s presence is itself a trial for wealthy opponents. «Nor should he turn away the poor among the believers merely to please these arrogant elements.» [filed under 6:51-55]
#104 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · The Prophet is not accountable for arrogant people’s refusal, and neither are they accountable for his duties in a way that could justify his turning believers away; doing so would be injustice. «Similarly, these people will not be held responsible on the Day of Judgement for the duties imposed on him»
#105 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · Muhammad must not abandon sincere worshippers to appease wealthy, arrogant people who disparage his poor companions. «he should not waste any more time on the wretched among them who are inebriated by their status»
<<part 2 ends; continues in part 3>>

<<notes for 6_52_c3, part 3 of 0..4>>
#106 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · Quraysh leaders disparaged the companions as poor menial workers and argued that respectable people could not join a religion that welcomed them; Muhammad must not lose true companions to win these elites. «his companions were all poor who did menial jobs and how could God select such lowly sections of the society for His religion»
#107 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · If the elites persist in error, they alone bear its consequence; turning away genuine seekers would leave the Prophet liable for neglecting those deserving his care. «If he goes after these wretched elements, they will not be held responsible on his behalf»
#108 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · Addressing Muhammad rather than the Quraysh directly strikes at their arrogance and implies they are unworthy of direct address. «instead of addressing them, the Prophet (sws) is addressed. This is to make evident to them that they are not even worthy of being addressed directly.»
#109 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · The verb used for driving the poor away is harsh and means to disregard someone disparagingly, matching what Quraysh wanted Muhammad to do to his companions. «it means to disparagingly disregard someone.»
#110 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · Jesus (sws) · reports · Jesus’ lost-sheep parable depicts a shepherd seeking one straying sheep instead of being content with the ninety-nine. «Jesus (sws) has stated a parable also: “What do you think? If a man owns a hundred sheep»
#111 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · The lost-sheep parable illustrates God’s affection for people who return after error and a prophet’s concern for his nation’s faith. «Just as this parable shows the great affection God has for people who turn to Him after being in error»
#112 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · The Prophet should warn those who fear God and the hereafter, ignore demands for miracles, and welcome poor believers seeking God’s pleasure without turning them away to attract arrogant elites. «As for those who seek God’s pleasure and want to listen to his message, he must not distance them from himself» [filed under 6:51-55]
#113 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · Prophetic concern for people reflects God’s affection and is praiseworthy, but it has limits: the Prophet must not pursue the wayward at the expense of loyal companions. «God does not want his prophet to go after those people who have gone astray at the expense of his real companions.»
#114 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · reports · Farāhī discusses important points on this topic in his commentary on Sūrah ‘Abas; Islahi says he will give his own view later. «Ustādh Far āhī has written some very important points related to this topic in his exegesis of Sūrah ‘Abas.»
#115 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · The poor believers seek only their Creator’s pleasure, so the promised mercy and forgiveness answer their actual desire rather than worldly status or riches. «The only desire they had was to please their creator and master.» [filed under 6:52, 6:54]
#116 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · reports · A report in Muslim and other hadith collections says Quraysh notables demanded the poor, vulnerable Companions leave before they would meet Muhammad; he refused, then considered their lesser demand before this verse stopped him. «Müslim’in Sahîh’i (“Fezâilü’s-sahâbe”, 45-46) ve diğer bazı hadis kaynaklarında yer alan bir rivayete göre»
#117 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · Habbâb · reports · After the verse, the Prophet and poor Muslims grew so close that they sat knee to knee, and he waited for them to rise before leaving so as not to hurt them. «Habbâb’ın anlattığına göre bu âyetin inmesinden sonra Hz. Peygamber’le yoksul ve kimsesiz müslümanlar arasındaki yakınlık o kadar artmıştır»
#118 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · müfessirlerin çoğu · rejects · Most commentators, noting reports that the whole surah descended at once rather than in parts, deny that this verse was occasioned by that incident; even if so, the incident only occasions its universal ethical teaching. «müfessirlerin çoğu bu sûrenin, parça parça değil, tamamının bir defada indiğini bildiren haberleri de dikkate alarak»
#119 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · some interpreters · reports · Some interpreters take the pronoun ‘they’ in the accountability clause to refer to the polytheists. «“Onların hesaplarından sana sorumluluk yoktur...” cümlesindeki “onlar” zamiriyle müşriklere işaret edildiğini düşünenler olmuşsa da»
#120 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · ağırlıklı görüş · prefers · The predominant view is that ‘they’ refers to the poor Muslims mentioned earlier. «ağırlıklı görüş, bununla yukarıda anılan müslümanların kastedildiği yönündedir»
#121 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · müşrikler · reports · The polytheists alleged that the poor Muslims gathered around the Prophet for shelter, food, and drink rather than sincere devotion. «Rivayete göre müşrikler, Hz. Peygamber’in çevresinde toplanan söz konusu kişilerin, aslında –samimi dindarlıklarından değil– barınma imkânı buldukları, yiyip içtikleri için orada toplandıklarını ileri sürmüşlerdi»
#122 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · one view · reports · One interpretation says the verse separates the Prophet’s responsibility from the poor Muslims’ responsibility: each bears their own deeds, so he should remain close to them rather than wrong them. «herkesin kendi yapıp ettiklerinin sorumluluğunu yine kendisinin taşıdığı bildirilerek Resûl-i Ekrem’in onlara olan ilgisini sürdürmesi istenmiş»
#123 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · another interpretation · reports · Another reading says the Prophet should not send worshipping poor people away to earn a living: their provision is God’s responsibility, not his calculation. «herkesin rızkını verenin Allah Teâlâ olduğuna işaret buyurulmuştur (Râzî, XII, 236-237)»
#124 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · holds · Human worth in Islam rests on faith, reverence for God, and spiritual nobility rather than rank, wealth, or lineage; the verse also shows the Prophet’s character formed by Qur’anic principles. «mevki, zenginlik ve soyuna göre değil iman zenginliğine, Allah’a saygı ve ruh yüceliğine göre değer taşıdığını ortaya koyması»
#125 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · holds · Humiliating people valued by God for faith and conduct is injustice, even if the hypothetical offender were a prophet. «farzımuhal bu kimse peygamber bile olsa– zalim olarak gösterilmesi son derece ilgi çekicidir»
#126 QIRAAT-ER · holds · Ghudwa as an instance noun contrasts with ghadāh as general morning, shifting from habitual to specific morning. «ghudwa (instance noun) vs ghadāh (general morning) — shifts from habitual to specific single-morning reading»
#127 STUDYQURAN · reports · Prominent Makkans wanted to join the Prophet’s teaching circle but disliked association with lower-status followers and asked him to send them away. «This verse was reportedly revealed when a group of prominent Makkans indicated that they wished to join the Prophet’s teaching circle»
#128 STUDYQURAN · al-Rāzī · reports · Al-Rāzī holds that the Prophet did not sin by initially appearing willing to accommodate the demand because his intention was good. «cannot be said to have sinned in his apparent initial willingness to accommodate the Makkans’ demand (R)»
#129 STUDYQURAN · R, Ṭ · reports · Morning and evening invocation may mean the five canonical prayers performed at their appointed times. «refer to praying the five canonical prayers at their prescribed times»
#130 STUDYQURAN · R, Ṭ · reports · Morning and evening invocation may mean supererogatory remembrance of God or Quran recitation. «performing supererogatory acts of invoking God»
#131 STUDYQURAN · R, Ṭ · reports · The invocation may include all these practices together. «or to all of them (R, Ṭ)»
#132 STUDYQURAN · R · reports · Desiring God’s Face can mean literally hoping to see it, as a sincere lover longs to see the beloved’s face. «with the hope of seeing God’s Face, for any sincere lover longs to see the face of the beloved (R)»
#133 STUDYQURAN · IK, R · reports · Desiring God’s Face can also metaphorically mean sincerity of intention among the Prophet’s followers. «it refers metaphorically to sincerity of intention among the Prophet’s followers (IK, R)»
#134 STUDYQURAN · holds · The verse echoes the Quranic principle that no person bears another’s burden. «echoes the Quranic idea that none shall bear the burden of another (6:164; 17:15; 35:18; 39:7; 53:38)»
#135 STUDYQURAN · Z · prefers · Syntactically, “their reckoning” most likely refers to the pious worshippers’ own reckoning, so the Prophet judges piety by outward acts. «that the Prophet need only judge his followers’ piety on the basis of their outward actions (Z)»
#136 STUDYQURAN · Some commentators · reports · Some commentators say the verse responds to a Quraysh accusation that the poor followed the Prophet for material support rather than religious sincerity. «Some commentators explain this as a response to an accusation made by some of the Quraysh»
#137 STUDYQURAN · R · reports · On that reading, the Prophet need not assess possible ulterior motives behind his followers’ apparent piety. «the verse was meant to indicate that the Prophet had no responsibility to assess the possible ulterior motives behind his»
#138 STUDYQURAN · Ṭ · reports · Some reports say the Makkans asked only that the poor followers be moved to the back rows of prayer, not expelled altogether. «Some reports indicate the Prophet was not asked to send away these followers altogether, but rather to send them to the back rows of prayer»
#139 STUDYQURAN · Z · prefers · More plausibly, the reckoning concerns the prominent Makkans; the Prophet need not court their conversion by yielding to their demand to dismiss sincere followers. «their embracing Islam that he should accede to their demand and “drive away”his pious followers at their behest (Z)»
<<part 3 ends; continues in part 4>>

<<notes for 6_52_c3, part 4 of 0..4>>
#140 STUDYQURAN · holds · The Prophet refused to drive away his poorer followers, as Noah refused similar demands, though he was prepared to have them depart temporarily when prominent Makkans visited. «The Prophet refused to “drive away” his poorer followers (in 11:27–29 and 26:111–14 Noah refuses to do the same)»
#141 STUDYQURAN · IK, R, Ṭ, W · reports · The verse was revealed to forbid the Prophet from driving away his pious followers who worship morning and evening. «This verse was then revealed forbidding him from “driving away” his pious followers who call upon their Lord morning and evening (IK, R, Ṭ, W)»
#142 STUDYQURAN · Ṭ, W · reports · Quran 18:28 is linked to a similar circumstance and is reportedly a revelation about that situation. «reportedly revealed in a similar circumstance (Ṭ, W)»
#143 STUDYQURAN · holds · Quran 80:1–10 recounts the incident in which the Prophet is admonished for showing displeasure when a poor blind man came instead of wealthier Makkans. «about the incident in which the Prophet is admonished for registering displeasure when his teaching attracted a poor blind man rather than the wealthier Makkans»
#144 STUDYQURAN · holds · These passages raise the question of how the Prophet could appear to favor status-conscious Makkans over sincere followers, given that driving them away would make him a wrongdoer. «These passages raise the question of how the Prophet could seem to favor these prominent Makkans»
#145 STUDYQURAN · al-Rāzī · reports · Al-Rāzī says the Prophet’s possible initial willingness to accommodate the Makkans was intended only to facilitate their acceptance of Islam. «al-Rāzī argues that even if the Prophet were initially prepared to accede to the Makkans’ demand»
#146 STUDYQURAN · al-Rāzī · reports · Al-Rāzī reasons that the poor followers could be instructed another time, so no spiritual harm would come to them. «his intention was only to facilitate their acceptance of Islam, and since the Prophet could continue to instruct his poorer followers at another time»
#147 STUDYQURAN · holds · Al-Anʿām is Makkan and addresses the Prophet and Muslims' struggle with Makkan idolatry; its central aim is to refute idolatry and invented ritual practices. «al-Anʿām clearly addresses the challenges faced by the Prophet and the Muslims engaged in a religious struggle with the idolatrous Makkans» [filed under 6:1-165]
#148 STUDYQURAN · holds · The surah refutes worship of idols, celestial bodies, and jinn, and challenges the Makkans' invented religious practices. «The primary concern of the sūrah is to refute through powerful arguments various kinds of idolatry in general—including the worship of idols, celestial bodies, and jinn» [filed under 6:1-165]
#149 STUDYQURAN · Many · reports · Many regard it as a late Makkan surah, reflecting the Prophet's final effort to persuade the Makkans before his 622 migration to Madinah. «Many consider this sūrah to be a late Makkan one and thus to reflect the culmination of the Prophet’s struggle and effort to persuade the Makkans» [filed under 6:1-165]
#150 STUDYQURAN · holds · The Prophet is addressed throughout and given arguments and challenges for disbelievers; the surah sums up the Quranic case against idolatry. «The Prophet is directly addressed throughout the sūrah and given specific arguments and challenges to pose to the disbelievers in Makkah» [filed under 6:1-165]
#151 STUDYQURAN · reports · A hadith reports that al-Anʿām descended all at once with seventy thousand angels praising and glorifying God. «According to a ḥadīth, “Sūrat al-Anʿām was sent down all at once, accompanied by seventy thousand angels, hymning glorifications and praises”» [filed under 6:1-165]
#152 STUDYQURAN · al-Zamakhsharī · reports · A longer version adds that the seventy thousand angels seek forgiveness for whoever recites al-Anʿām with each verse, day and night. «A longer version of thisḥadīth cited by al-Zamakhsharī adds» [filed under 6:1-165]
<<end of notes for 6_52_c3>>
